title: Security-group change removes egress rule to the external payment processor
source_note: Failure pattern (an infrastructure access-control change silently removes a required network path to a critical dependency, so connections time out while DNS still resolves) is a common operational class discussed in the Google SRE Book. All services, change IDs, log lines, metrics, and timestamps are fabricated for evaluation.
incident_report: Since ~11:07 UTC all card payments are failing at checkout with 'try again later'. Non-payment traffic is fine. No application deploys. Cloud infra team pushed a security-group change this morning.

signal_lines.msg: security group sg-pay-egress updated: 1 rule removed, 2 added (change CR-4821)
outbound connection to processor.acme-pay.com timing out (connect timeout 10s)
100% of payment authorizations failing: upstream connect timeout
DNS resolves processor.acme-pay.com fine; TCP connect never completes
payment step failing; showing 'try again later' to users
CR-4821 rolled back; egress rule for the processor CIDR restored

ground_truth.root_cause: A security-group change (CR-4821) intended to tighten egress rules removed the rule permitting payments-gateway to reach the external payment processor's IP range. DNS still resolved, but TCP connections to the processor could no longer be established, so every payment authorization timed out. Non-payment traffic was unaffected. Recovery required rolling back the change.
evidence_path: cloud-infra INFO at 11:05: security group sg-pay-egress updated (CR-4821), one rule removed
payments-gateway outbound connections to the processor start timing out at 11:07
payments-gateway notes DNS resolves but TCP connect never completes - a network-path failure, not a DNS failure
payment_auth_success_rate falls to 0 and outbound connect errors spike
recovery after CR-4821 is rolled back at ~11:25
ground_truth.fix: Roll back CR-4821 (done). Review security-group changes that affect payment egress against a known-good allowlist, test them in staging, and add synthetic monitoring that authorizes a test transaction end to end.
